analysis:
This unit contains docs and changelog only. No source for the described provider changes is included, so the implementation is unreviewed.

The changelog and docs describe:
- A protocol-1 endpoint-custody response for same-process reconnects. It uses a fresh per-socket nonce and the in-memory X25519 key, with no Apple work or local trust grant (provider.md head 66-77; attestation.md patch hunk at head ~68).
- A logout change that drains the provider and attempts token revocation.
- An opt-in signed-app native qualification diagnostic.

The main security-relevant change is in docs/architecture/security/attestation.md, head line 112. It declares that platform authorization (EvaluateAuthorization) no longer needs a verified risk receipt for basic serving, and that an established identity may retain last-known policy on failed administrative reads within ceilings. It links an external platform commit that cannot be verified here. This contradicts the canonical threat-model statements that every grant needs a fresh verified receipt (T-053/T-055/T-057, TB-011). threat-model.yaml is not updated in this PR (reported as a finding).

Assumptions for the next pass:
- The endpoint-resumption responder must not sign or decrypt attacker-chosen data. The nonce and origin binding must stop replay or cross-socket reuse, and resume state must be cleared on teardown (CoordinatorClient.connectAndRun).
- Logout must not leave a token valid. Revocation against the running provider's coordinator, including command-line overrides, could be directed at a malicious URL, so credentials must not be sent to non-allowlisted hosts (T-017-like SSRF).
- The native qualification diagnostic must not grant serving.

The code implementing these is not supplied.

findings.detail: The PR rewrites the attestation Context paragraph to follow a platform contract. Under it, missing recurring receipt/risk evidence "neither blocks otherwise qualified basic serving nor adds assertions". It also lets an established exact identity "retain last-known policy" when administrative reads fail, up to the proof and administrative ceilings. The canonical threat model (TB-011, T-053/T-055/T-057, header notes) still says every serving grant needs a fresh verified risk receipt, and treats receipts as part of the sybil/continuity defense. The PR does not touch threat-model.yaml, although a changelog line claims the retained threat model stays aligned. The assumptions are now inconsistent. Basic serving can proceed without receipt evidence, which weakens the throttle on credential rotation and fake-machine inflation (T-055). Revocation or denial can lag by the retained-policy window when reads fail (T-053). Fix: update TB-011 and T-053/T-055/T-057, plus A-016, to the receipt-optional basic grant. State the maximum retained-policy and revocation lag, and keep reward and MDM-removal readiness explicitly receipt-gated. Alternatively, mark the doc text as a platform-repo contract that is not yet adopted here.
findings.title: Docs adopt receipt-optional basic serving, but the threat model still requires a verified risk receipt
